consumer: An engine possession predicate over the avatar's on-person inventory (e.g. Character::has_charges("9mm",30)/charges_of("9mm")) asking 'does the avatar have >=30 rounds of 9mm on their person?'
scope: On-person possession only (wielded/worn/inventory), counting ammo recursively including rounds nested in magazines/containers, returning the engine's own threshold verdict
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_carried_items dumps raw per-item rows (type_id, charges, count_by_charges) and leaves the threshold un-computed, so the frontend must re-derive the answer from a partial view
divergence: Avatar carries 40 rounds of 9mm loaded inside a magazine that sits in a wielded/holstered pistol: the engine's has_charges counts those rounds (verdict yes), but summing carried_items[].charges over flat rows misses ammo nested in the magazine/gun and reports a false 'no'
